240-geography: 24 GEOG credits chosen with the Adviser, not GEOG 200 or 205, at most 6 at 200.
240-outside-geography: 9 credits at 300 or 400+ from other units in humanities, social and physical sciences or engineering, related to your focus and approved by the Adviser.
240-program-description: More focused than the Major, with a 6-credit thesis. Keep CGPA 3.00 and program GPA 3.30. 500-level seminars encouraged. Up to 30 credits outside Arts and Science. Follow course levels: 200 in U1, 300 in U2, 400–500 in U3.
241-remaining-courses: 18 credits, at least 12 at 300+ and 6 outside Geography.
241-architecture: Prerequisites waived, but not before U3.
242-additional-courses: 6 credits at 300+, from these lists or others with your adviser.
242-program-description: Combine Geography with another Arts discipline, including a two-semester original research project. Requirements vary by unit, so see an adviser in each. Keep CGPA 3.00 and program GPA 3.30.
242-research: 3–6 credits. If both require a thesis, submit to either; if to the other, register for GEOG 492D. Sometimes jointly supervised.
242-geography: 12–15 coherent GEOG credits approved by the Adviser, not GEOG 200 or 205, at most 6 at 200. A field course is desirable.
243-about-history: Cultures and societies worldwide from antiquity to now, plus theory, sexuality, imperialism, science, environment and ideas. Builds research, writing and critical skills for law, business, journalism, academia, finance, government, the arts, education and medicine.
243-programs-in-history: Minor, Major, Honours and Joint Honours, all with advanced-level minimums, and breadth for all but the minor. Meet an adviser regularly.
AP and IB credits don't count toward History program credits, but may meet prerequisites for upper-level courses; ask the professor or adviser.
243-about-classical-studies: Languages, literature, history and culture of ancient Greece and Rome, through CLAS, ancient HIST, and related Philosophy, English and Art History courses.
Minor and Major complement other studies; Honours and Joint Honours lay foundations for academic careers and graduate or professional school.
243-about-south-asian-studies: Offered with Anthropology, English, History, Political Science, Sociology, Islamic Studies and Religious Studies. Two streams: Culture and Civilization (India, Pakistan, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan) or Languages (Persian, Sanskrit, Tibetan, Urdu-Hindi). Adviser: Prof. Andrea Farran.
243-location: Leacock Building, Room 712, 855 Sherbrooke St. W.
244-program-description: An introduction to cultures and societies worldwide, a good complement to Arts majors, expandable to the Major. See an adviser early in first year and fill out an audit form. AP and IB credits don't count.
244-complementary-courses-18-credits: HIST or cognate, at most 6 at 200.
244-cognate-courses: Non-HIST courses count up to 3 credits. Others can go to the Undergraduate Program Director. A course counts toward only one program, and 200-level cognates count toward the 200-level limit.
244-program-description-2: Flexible breadth and depth, with historical theory and methods, designed around your geographic, chronological or thematic interests. See an adviser early in first year with an audit form. AP and IB credits don't count.
244-complementary-courses-36-credits: Distribution: 3 credits each from Groups A, B and C (no cognates). Temporal: at least 3 before 1800 and 3 after, not with HIST 299; one course can meet both.
Levels: at most 15 at 200, at least 6 at 400–500, with at most 3 from HIST 498 or 499.
245-cognate-courses-max-6-credits: Others can go to the Undergraduate Program Director. A course counts toward only one program.
246-program-description: In-depth training in methods and research, especially for graduate study. See an adviser early in first year with an audit form. AP and IB credits don't count.
246-complementary-courses-51-credits: Same distribution and temporal rules (not HIST 299 or 399 for temporal). At least 6 credits of honours seminars (500-level D1/D2), 6 more at 400+, at most 18 at 200.
GPA: 3.30 in program courses, B or higher in each, CGPA 3.0+.
247-cognate-courses-max-9-credits: Others can go to the Director. 200-level ones count toward the 18-credit limit.
247-program-description: Breadth, depth, methods and research, combined with another Arts discipline, whose requirements you also meet. See an adviser early with an audit form. AP and IB credits don't count.
247-complementary-courses-33-credits: Same distribution and temporal rules. At least 6 credits of honours seminars, 3 more at 400–500, at most 12 at 200.
GPA: 3.30 in program courses, B or higher in each, CGPA 3.0+.
248-cognate-courses-max-6-credits: Others can go to the Director. 200-level ones count toward the 12-credit limit.
249-program-description: Language, history and culture of Greece and Rome, expandable to the Major.
249-complementary-courses-15-credits: At least 6 of Ancient Greek or Latin, 3 CLAS at 400, at most 9 at 200, at most 6 of non-CLAS or transfer.
249-program-description-2: Classical Languages stream: advanced Greek, Latin or both. Classical Studies stream: broad foundation, with more courses in translation.
249-classical-languages-stream: 33 credits, at least 6 advanced Greek or Latin, at most 12 at 200, at most 9 non-CLAS.
249-classical-studies-stream: 6 from the first list; 27 more, at least 6 intermediate Greek or Latin, 6 CLAS at 400, at most 12 at 200, at most 9 non-CLAS.
In either stream, at most 12 non-CLAS and transfer in total.
250-program-description: For graduate study in Classics or related fields: proficiency in Greek and Latin, advanced in at least one, with ancient history, literature and material culture. Start both languages early. Keep CGPA and program GPA 3.00.
250-complementary-courses-30-credits: At least 6 advanced Greek or Latin, 3 advanced literature, 3 ancient history or civilization, 3 art or archaeology. Others with adviser approval. At most 18 at 200, and 18 non-CLAS and transfer.
251-program-description: Proficiency in Greek and Latin, advanced in at least one, for graduate study in Classics, ancient history or similar. Keep CGPA and program GPA 3.00.
251-complementary-courses-24-credits: At least 6 advanced Greek or Latin, at most 15 at 200, 9 non-CLAS, and 12 non-CLAS and transfer in total.
252-program-description: History, literature, languages, politics, religions and cultures of South Asia, in two streams, taught across departments with instruction in Persian, Sanskrit, Tibetan and Urdu-Hindi.
252-stream-1-culture-and-civilization: Course content changes, so have courses approved by the adviser, and check prerequisites.
252-intermediate-and-advanced-curriculum: 12 credits. Adviser may add courses. At most 6 from exchange, and up to 6 of language with approval.
253-stream-2-language: 18 credits in one of Persian, Sanskrit, Tibetan or Urdu-Hindi, or 6 in one and 12 in another. Check prerequisites.
253-urdu-hindi: Adviser may add courses. At most 6 from exchange.
254-about-information-studies: Educates information professionals and scholars, with a human-centred approach to managing and preserving knowledge. At McGill since 1897, Canada's first such school, A.L.A. accredited since 1929.
Graduate only: Master of Information Studies, certificates and Ph.D. Research on human-computer interaction, information behaviour and knowledge management.
255-about-world-islamic-and-middle-east-: Language-based interdisciplinary training on Muslim societies and their neighbours, across times and places, with Arabic, Persian, Turkish or Urdu, and courses in history, law, religion, philosophy, art, literature, gender, politics and anthropology.
Major, minor, honours, joint honours, and language minors. You must have been offered admission to a McGill bachelor's program.
255-about-african-studies: Since 1969, Canada's first, with courses across disciplines leading to a minor, major and joint honours on politics, history, society, economy and environment.
Starts with an interdisciplinary introduction and ends with a research seminar. Includes Swahili, travel and study in Africa, and activities with ASSA and MASS.
255-program-description: For Arts majors wanting interdisciplinary knowledge of Africa, expandable to the Major.
256-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from Group A and 9 from Group B across at least 2 disciplines, at most 6 from one. The adviser can modify if courses aren't offered, or approve other courses with African content.
256-group-b: From at least 2 disciplines, at most 6 from one.
256-english: Counts only when African materials are taught.
257-program-description: Interdisciplinary study of the continent. See the Adviser at the start of first year, and focus on one discipline as you can.
257-complementary-courses-30-credits: 9 from Group A and 21 from Group B across at least 3 disciplines, at most 9 from one. The adviser can modify or approve others.
257-group-b: From at least 3 disciplines, at most 9 from one.
258-program-description: Combine with another Arts discipline, seeing advisers in each about courses and any thesis. Program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00. At least 9 of 36 credits at 400+.
258-required-courses-9-credits: The Honours Thesis (AFRI 480) is required, on top of what your second program demands.
259-geography: Normally field courses in the African Studies Field Semester.
259-political-science: Counts only when African materials are taught. Admission depends on Political Science and its Honours Adviser, with priority for its students.
259-program-description: Listening, speaking, reading and writing in Arabic. Can expand to the WIMES Major.
